title: Sequenced KV fragment pipeline and graceful cardinality degradation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Design and implement a sequenced fragment-processing pipeline for paged/blocked KV that reduces GPU tail latency under continuous batching while allowing controlled, graceful degradation when overall KV cardinality exceeds resident budgets. This ticket focuses on the in-memory fragment queue, deterministic slot propagation, a lightweight resident-score for admission, and a spillback policy that prefers whole-fragment demotion over fine-grained single-block evictions to keep batch semantics stable.

Goals:
- Keep 95th/99th percentile token latency within current SLOs under bursty multi-tenant workloads.
- Avoid pathological OOMs by providing a predictable degradation path (cardinality reduction) rather than opportunistic evictions that break KV lookups.
- Integrate with continuous batching so that batching heuristics are aware of fragment residency and can prefer cache-affine batches.
- Expose telemetry and lightweight knobs for production rollouts and rapid iteration.

Design overview:
- Fragment unit: treat a contiguous set of KV entries created by a generation as a single "fragment" header with metadata (creation_seq, token_range, resident_score, last_used_ts). Fragments are the atomic unit for coalescing, migration, and spillback.
- Sequenced fragment queue: an append-only ring that preserves allocation order for prefetched fragments. Each fragment entry contains a short bloom-ish fingerprint and an occupancy bitmap (block-level) to speed host/GPU residency checks without full deserialization.
- Resident-score: a compact uint8 score computed from frequency histogram, last_used delta, and token affinity. Score used by admission and quick hotset heuristics. Scores decay with an exponential backoff to prefer recent activity.
- Slot propagation: fragments map to a small fixed-size slot table (power-of-two buckets) on the host. Slot entries point to host staging pages; a GPU-residency bit, a sequence counter, and a soft-lock token used by the runtime during batching to avoid mid-batch migrations.
- Coalescing strategy: when reclaiming, prefer demoting entire fragments that have low resident-score and low predicted future access (based on sequence and histogram) rather than evicting individual blocks across many fragments. This reduces read-amplification and kernel churn.
- Spillback policy: host-side async spillback with two classes: eager (for sustained oversubscription) and opportunistic (short bursts). Eager spillback uses a throttled background writer; opportunistic spillback is inline but limited to small fraction of batch time budget.

Integration with continuous batching and runtime:
- Batch planner reads a per-worker hotset sample and biases request coalescing toward fragments with resident_score >= threshold. This increases cache hit-rate for active batches.
- During batch scheduling, fragments with soft-lock tokens are treated as "pinned" for the duration of the batch to prevent eviction-induced tail spikes. The pin is best-effort and expires at end of batch.
- Batcher fallbacks: if hotset hit-rate drops beneath configured target and resident memory is saturated, batcher reduces max batch size for the affected worker group and signals the eviction controller to accelerate whole-fragment demotion.

Telemetry and observability:
- New metrics: fragment_coalesce_count, fragment_demote_rate, resident_score_histogram, spillback_write_latency_p50/p95, batch_affinity_hit_rate, soft_lock_conflicts, fragment_reconstruction_time.
- Tracing hooks: annotate request spans with fragment IDs and residency state so end-to-end token latency can be decomposed into usgc (user-space GC), fragment_fetch, kernel_execute.
- Alerts: sustained fragment_demote_rate or reduced batch_affinity_hit_rate will open a mitigation runbook.

API/Config knobs (runtime-configurable):
- fragment_min_size_bytes (default 8KB)
- resident_score_threshold (default 32)
- eager_spillback_enabled (true/false)
- max_pinned_fragments_per_worker (default 64)
- batch_affinity_min_hit_rate (default 0.6)

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit tests for slot-table concurrency (simulate concurrent pin/demote cycles).
- Microbench harness: synthetic workload with controlled cardinality spikes, measuring p50/p95/p99 token latency and kernel churn with and without fragment coalescing.
- Dogfood: enable feature behind flag on a small set of Dedicated nodes with cap on memory overhead and strict telemetry.
- Chaos: inject delayed spillback writes and verify graceful degradation path (cardinality reduction and batch-size trimming) does not cause request failures.

Rollout & migration plan:
1) Feature gated runtime-binary with fragment pipeline disabled by default.
2) Enable on internal canary cluster; collect metrics for one week.
3) Enable opportunistic spillback and small pinned fragment budget in canary.
4) Gradually increase pin budget and enable eager spillback on low-load regions.
5) Public rollout behind runtime-1.21 with opt-in flag per-customer; provide migration doc for Dedicated/Private customers.

Open questions / trade-offs considered:
- Fragment granularity: smaller fragments reduce wasted host memory but increase metadata overhead and lock contention. Chosen default favors slightly larger fragments to reduce kernel churn.
- Demote whole-fragment vs block eviction: whole-fragment demotion is simpler and produces more stable latencies but may increase spillback IO for hot-but-sparse fragments. We will revisit if telemetry shows high write amplification.
- Soft-lock model: best-effort pins may delay eviction but could also increase temporary resident working set; bounded pin count avoids runaway memory growth.

comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha Patel: Initial draft of fragment pipeline design posted. Focused on deterministic pinning and whole-fragment demotion to keep tail latency predictable. Added resident_score concept to simplify admission policy.

2026-02-25 - Marco Chen: Reviewed. Agree with whole-fragment demotion for now; flagged concern about write amplification for sparse fragments. Suggested adding occupancy bitmap to fragment header so we can cheaply estimate IO cost before demoting.

2026-03-02 - Lena Ortiz (Perf): Ran microbench with prototype coalescer. Observed 18% reduction in p99 under synthetic chat-like workload with ~200k cardinality; write amplification increased ~7% for certain traces. Attached perf logs to the PR.
2026-03-05 - Marco Chen: Implemented slot table soft-lock and pinned fragment limit. Added fast-path resident check using 64-bit fingerprint. Pushed WIP PR 2483; awaiting CI.
2026-03-09 - Security (Yvonne Kim): Quick review: no new secret paths. Ensure spillback writer honors KMS/HSM policies for Private deployments (note added to PR).

2026-03-11 - Aisha Patel: Updated ticket with rollout plan and metrics. Moving to In Progress. Next: finalize async spillback throttle and add observability dashboards for fragment_reconstruction_time.
